correctness.rationale: For k>=2 half-translation splits the N-dimensional function space into exactly N/2-dimensional eigenspaces. Within a parity sector, when the b-parities disagree the exact complete-square Gauss sum has squared magnitude 2N and cannot vanish. Fixed chirps identify each sector with the lower-modulus system; this is both necessary and sufficient, and unique. At k=1 parity of a+b gives four bases. Recursion B_k=4B_(k-1)^2 yields 2^(2^(k+1)-2). A standard-library exact checker verifies all 2^(2k) Gauss sums for k<=5 and independently exhausts bases for k<=3; no infinite conclusion is inferred from finite tests.
